I live & grew up outside Philly. I always heard the PA road jokes w/o any personal experiences elsewhere to compare it to. We once drove to VT & spent a good deal of it on NY Thruway (287?) & wow, it was eye opening. The Schuykill or 95 would be equivalent of sleeping on a fold out where the thruway was sleeping on a 5-Star hotel's mattress.
I'm beaming w/ pride. Great work & my favorite era of Jerry. Keep it up.

Ha. I interviewed McNally for a college paper in early 2000s & got a cliff notes telling of this story.

I wore out 2 tapes of this. The 1st I got was just labeled "Lonesome Prison Blues" & Iistened to it end over end for weeks. The R&C is so perfect, but "Run for the Roses" catches so much emotion for me at that time. I really felt like that was written for beta-male me. On some psycho Manson/Lennon/McCartney vibe, I thought he was singing my life. He was.   "Just want the cup, but don't want the race..."

When there was no ear to hear
You sang to me

I struggle w/ those thoughts too. Always have. It's really just shitty problem solving, speaking for me. If you flip the board during a losing game, you're just ensuring one thing...the loss. There's a lot to life that can lessen the bullshit & I doubt those options for enjoyment exist in death. Stick around. Find games you win for yourself & by yourself. Find some new favorite anythings. I also highly suggest reading as much Vonnegut as you can. Life is one of the worst things that has happened to me, in all honesty, but sitting in an empty theater w/ no movie-ever playing ever-seems dull. Especially forever. Forever ever....

Seriously, homes. Reach out to me anytime. I'll happily give you my phone number if it will help you in the least. You're not alone & you're better than the thoughts holding you back. Internet hugs.
I was at 6-18 show. My last...
Looked for Vonnegut. Not disappointed.
Exactly what I was wondering...

Tiger is like one of the cool uncles that snuck me some beers or hits on a joint at those big family cookouts. The coming alive memories of 80s/90s are scarred w/ Tiger's claws. Gorgeous & wouldn't change a thing.

But...

Wolf is the grandfather that was mastering the grill all along. Stoking fire, turning meat, unfiltered in his lips, swatting away greedy hands, & offering mindfood that doesn't taste anywhere near the same at any another family's picnic.

Wolf gets my vote.
Every era shines at times.
I don't get it...
